meta.title: MLflow Run Migration: The Two Defaults That Silently Under-Deliver

views.label: search_runs caps at 1000
views.note: An experiment with 5,000 runs migrates 1,000 of them and reports success unless the page_token is followed.

views.label: metrics holds the latest value, not the series
views.note: Re-logging from run.data.metrics turns a 200-epoch curve into a single point — get_metric_history is the real series.

views.label: The run ID map is the deliverable
views.note: Model registry migration needs the migrated run ID, not the source one — nothing produces this map for you.

segments.label: Re-log and hand off the ID map

cards.title: Two defaults that pass a demo and fail a real experiment
items: run.data.metrics is the latest value per key, not the series — a training curve collapses to one point
search_runs caps at 1000 and pages via page_token — an unpaginated script silently drops the rest
Both fail silently: the target has runs, the counts just don't match unless someone checks

cards.title: parentRunId needs its own remap
items: mlflow.* tags are system-managed and get filtered out of a naive tag copy
parentRunId is one of them — re-set it explicitly, remapped through run_id_map
Parents must migrate before their children or the remap has nothing to point at yet

cards.title: The run ID map is the actual deliverable
items: Nothing produces this mapping automatically — the script has to build and keep it
Model registry re-registration needs the migrated run ID, not the source one
Print or persist run_id_map before the script exits; it's the handoff artifact
